jobs.description:
Do you want to set the technical direction and design Business Central solutions that hold up in practice?

Kolding harbour with a tall ship, warehouses and reflections in the water — a few metres from DynaFlow’s offices

Our offices sit a few metres from the waterfront in Kolding.

At DynaFlow we are looking for a Solution Architect who wants to set the technical direction and help build one of the strongest Business Central environments in the country. We bring many years of experience from larger consultancies, and we use it to design solutions that hold up — even when the landscape is complex.

About DynaFlow

At DynaFlow we believe in a different way of being a consultancy. Good advice does not start with technology, PowerPoints or processes — it starts with people, business and understanding.

We specialise in Dynamics NAV and Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and have gathered more than 50 years of combined experience with solutions across industries, countries and organisations. Our clients range from large international groups to small and medium-sized businesses. For us, quality matters more than quantity, and we never leave a client stranded on the quayside.

About the role

As a Solution Architect you become the professional anchor when solutions are designed and the architecture is set. You translate the client’s business into robust, maintainable Business Central solutions — and you are the one colleagues and partners spar with when things get complex.

You work closely with consultants and developers, set the technical direction and make sure the solutions make sense both now and in the longer term. You get plenty of freedom to shape how we build.

Your tasks will include:

• Designing solutions and architecture that match the client’s business

• Technical direction and quality assurance across projects

• Breaking complex ERP landscapes into robust, maintainable solutions

• Sparring with other Business Central partners on complex tasks

• Professional sparring partner for consultants and developers

• Helping develop DynaFlow’s technical foundation, methods and standards

We imagine that you

• Have deep technical experience with Business Central/NAV, ideally at least 5 years

• Can design architecture and set technical direction in complex solutions

• Turn business needs into durable technical solutions

• Take independent ownership of quality, direction and momentum

• Communicate clearly with management, key users, developers and partners alike

• Thrive with freedom under responsibility, and bring humour and team spirit

• Speak and write fluent Danish, and preferably English

What we offer

• A central technical role in an ambitious, growing Business Central company

• The chance to help build one of the strongest Business Central environments in the country

• Plenty of freedom to set direction and shape how we build

• Complex work for both international groups and small/medium-sized businesses

• Skilled colleagues with deep consulting and business experience

• A strong team culture with room for humour, sparring and professional growth

• The option to work from home and flexible working hours

• Canteen lunch scheme

• Pension with a health-insurance scheme

• Paid phone and internet

• Premium offices a few metres from the waterfront in Kolding

How to apply

Send your application and CV to kontakt@dynaflow.dk. We invite candidates to interviews on a rolling basis, so don’t hesitate to reach out.

If you have questions about the position, you are very welcome to call Chris or Rasmus. We look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026 – Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU), Copenhagen, Denmark
jobs.description:
The Position:

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is seeking candidates for its newly established Supply Chain Internship Roster 2026. These internship opportunities are on-site at SCMU’s office in the UN City headquarters in Copenhagen, Denmark.

SCMU offers specialized functional streams aligned with its operational needs, including:

• Data & Analytics

• Logistics & Supply Chain

• Procurement & Business

• Humanitarian Supplies

• Supply Chain & Customer Service

• Governance, Risk & Compliance

• Communications

• Human Resources

• Information and Communications Technology (ICT)

• Administration & Business

To ensure effective team integration and maximize the value of the internship, candidates must be logistically and financially prepared to undertake full-time, on-site work in Copenhagen for the duration of the internship.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead UN agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every childbirth is safe and every young person's potential is fulfilled.  UNFPA’s strategic plan (2026-2029), reaffirms the relevance of the current strategic direction of UNFPA and focuses on three transformative results: to end preventable maternal deaths; end unmet need for family planning; and end gender-based violence and harmful practices. These results capture our strategic commitments on accelerating progress towards realizing the ICPD and SDGs in the Decade of Action leading up to 2030. Our strategic plan calls upon UN Member States, organizations and individuals to “build forward better”, while addressing the negative impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on women’s and girls’ access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights, recover lost gains and realize our goals.

The UNFPA Supply Chain Management Unit (SCMU) is self-funded and was made operational in January 2022. It is tasked with ensuring that UNFPA is able to effectively and efficiently support the delivery of life-saving reproductive health products and other programme supplies to the end user when and where they are needed. To achieve this, it is important to strengthen the capacity of governments and implementing partners to ensure coordination, end-to-end visibility and accountability on all supply chain and logistics management related activities, in particular for programme supplies, across all UNFPA programmes.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff, who embody these international norms and standards, and who will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates that transform, inspire and deliver high impact and sustained results; we need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them and who commit to deliver excellence in programme results.

Eligibility:

Educational requirements

a. Be enrolled in a first university degree programme (such as bachelor’s degree or equivalent) and have completed one full academic year;

b. Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (such as master’s programme or higher);

c. Have recently graduated with a university degree as defined above and, if selected, must start the internship within one-year of graduation; or

d. Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional trainee programme and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Other eligibility requirements

e. Demonstrate interest in the field of development;

f.  Demonstrate written and spoken proficiency in at least one of the working languages of the United Nations (English or French) and fluency in the official language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish) of the UNFPA office; and

g. Demonstrate ability to adapt to new environments and to establish and maintain good working relations with individuals of different cultural backgrounds.

An individual whose father, mother, son, daughter, brother or sister is a UNFPA staff member is not eligible for an internship with UNFPA.

Required Competencies:

Values:

• Exemplifying integrity,

• Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,

• Embracing cultural diversity,

• Embracing change

Core Competencies:

• Achieving results,

• Being accountable,

• Developing and applying professional expertise/business acumen,

• Thinking analytically and strategically,

• Working in teams/managing ourselves and our relationships,

Financial Support:

Interns who do not receive financial support from an outside party (such as an academic institution, university, government) are eligible to receive a stipend as a contribution towards living expenses. The stipend is based on the intern’s agreed place of work, which may be different from the duty station of the hiring office in cases of remote arrangements. The stipend is normally paid in local currency at the end of each month.

UNFPA Work Environment:

UNFPA provides a work environment that reflects the values of gender equality, diversity, integrity and healthy work-life balance. We are committed to ensuring gender parity in the organization and therefore encourage women to apply. Individuals from the LGBTQIA+ community, minority ethnic groups, indigenous populations, persons with disabilities, and other underrepresented groups are highly encouraged to apply. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. UNFPA promotes equal opportunities in terms of appointment, training, compensation and selection for all regardless of personal characteristics and dimensions of diversity. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion is at the heart of UNFPA's workforce - click here to learn more.

Disclaimer:

UNFPA does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process and does not concern itself with information on applicants' bank accounts.

Are you an experienced power trader who enjoys making decisions in fast-moving markets? Would you like to take responsibility for your own trades while working alongside colleagues who share your interest in intraday power trading?

Join our IDE Proprietary Trading team at Norlys Energy Trading in Aalborg. Here, you will use your trading experience to identify opportunities, act on market developments, and contribute to the team's trading activities.

Your team and role

You will join a team of experienced traders working in the intraday power market. The role combines market analysis, trade execution, and risk management with the development of trading strategies.

The desk operates around the clock, and you will be part of our 24/7 shift rotation. You will work independently on trading decisions while exchanging market insights and ideas with colleagues across shifts.

Your key responsibilities

• Analyse market data and price movements to identify trading opportunities.

• Develop and execute intraday trading strategies.

• Monitor positions, manage risk, and respond to changing market conditions.

• Collaborate with traders, analysts and quantitative teams to challenge market views, share insights, and improve trading strategies and decision-making.

• Contribute to improving trading tools, models and processes in collaboration with relevant teams to strengthen analytical capabilities and trading efficiency.

• Coordinate with colleagues across shifts to ensure continuity in trading activities.

• Maintain relationships with relevant market participants and stakeholders.

You'll be joining a desk where different perspectives and trading ideas are part of the conversation. There's room to share your experience, challenge ideas and learn from the people around you.

Jacob Goth

Manager, Proprietary Trading

What we are looking for

We are looking for an experienced trader who combines sound market judgement with the ability to act independently and contribute to a team.

You bring:

• Experience in energy trading, preferably within intraday power.

• Strong analytical skills and a solid understanding of trading strategies and risk management.

• The ability to make well-founded decisions under pressure.

• Good communication skills and an interest in sharing knowledge with colleagues.

• A relevant degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering or a related field.

You should be comfortable working in a 24/7 shift rotation and ready to apply your trading experience from an early stage.

What we offer

You will become part of a specialist trading environment where colleagues share market knowledge, discuss trading ideas, and learn from each other's experience. With responsibility for your own trading activities and opportunities to contribute to strategy development, you will have room to put your expertise to work.

Beyond the trading desk, you will be part of Norlys Energy Trading's wider professional and social community, including an active staff association that brings colleagues together across teams.

The position is permanent, full-time and based at our office in Aalborg, with an expected start date of 1 February 2027.

Interested?

If the role sounds like a good match for your experience, we'd like to hear from you.

Want to know more?

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about this opportunity

Jacob Goth

Manager, Proprietary Trading

Are you passionate about contemporary design and bringing innovative lighting products to life?

Do you have a technical background and experience developing products from concept to production?

Would you like to join a creative and international team in the heart of Copenhagen?

If yes, please read on!

PRODUCT DEVELOPER – LIGHTING

Based in Copenhagen

At our office in the heart of Copenhagen, you will join our Lighting Product Development team, working closely with talented designers, colleagues across different functions and international manufacturing partners. You will play a key role in transforming creative ideas into high-quality lighting products that combine design, functionality and technical excellence.

About the job

As Product Developer – Lighting at HAY, you will be involved in developing decorative LED lighting products from initial concept to final production. Combining technical development skills with a strong understanding of design, you will work closely with designers, internal teams and international manufacturing partners to bring creative ideas to life.

An important part of your role will be to maintain the original design intent throughout the development process, while ensuring that products meet technical requirements and can be manufactured efficiently. You will help drive projects forward, balancing design, functionality, quality, cost and timelines.

Your daily tasks will include:

• Manage product development projects from initial concept to production, ensuring timelines and key deliverables are met.

• Develop decorative LED lighting solutions, including optics, thermal management, drivers and dimming technologies.

• Create detailed, production-ready 3D models, assemblies and technical drawings using SolidWorks.

• Translate design concepts into technically feasible products, developing and testing prototypes and resolving technical and manufacturing challenges.

• Prepare technical specifications, bills of materials (BOMs) and test documentation.

• Ensure compliance with relevant electrical, safety, sustainability and regulatory requirements.

• Collaborate with designers, internal teams and external manufacturing partners throughout the development process.

• Manage project timelines, costs and technical deliverables, supporting suppliers with tooling, pilot production and quality control.

• Format 2D documentation utilizing Microsoft and Adobe Creative Suite packages.

Are you the Product Developer we are looking for?

We are looking for a technically skilled Product Developer who is passionate about contemporary design and has an eye for detail. You understand how to translate creative ideas into functional products without compromising the designer's original vision. You combine technical knowledge with a practical, solution-oriented approach and enjoy working at the intersection of design, engineering and manufacturing. You are comfortable taking responsibility for your projects, keeping track of timelines and collaborating with colleagues and external partners to find the best solutions.

Role expectations

• You are structured and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.

• You enjoy collaborating with designers, colleagues and external partners.

• You are a team player who values collaboration and contributes positively to the HAY culture.

Experience required

• You have a relevant educational background in Product Development, Industrial Design, Engineering or a related field.

• You have experience in technical product development, ideally taking products from concept to production. Experience within decorative lighting is an advantage.

• You have technical knowledge of LED lighting and an understanding of relevant electrical, safety and regulatory requirements.

• You are proficient in SolidWorks, including 3D modeling, assemblies and technical drawings.

• You have experience with prototyping, testing and technical documentation, along with an understanding of materials, manufacturing processes and supplier collaboration.

• You are familiar with Microsoft Office and Adobe Creative Suite for preparing and formatting product documentation.

• You communicate confidently in English, both written and spoken, as we are an international company.

You want to be a part of HAY?

Then do not hesitate to send us your application and CV, along with a portfolio showcasing relevant product development projects, as soon as possible and no later than Wednesday 18 November. We evaluate candidates on an ongoing basis.

If you have any further questions regarding the position, please do not hesitate to contact Recruiter, John Cain at john_cain@hermanmiller.com or Senior Manager, Sam Weller at sam.weller@hay.com.

Why join us?

Founded in Copenhagen in 2002 with the ambition of creating contemporary furniture, lighting and accessories for modern living, HAY’s vision is to create high-quality and well-designed products in collaboration with some of the world’s most talented, curious, and courageous designers. Through the commitment to sophisticated industrial manufacturing processes, HAY strives to make good design accessible to the widest possible audience.

Your closest partners will include senior scientific and business leaders across R&D, technology and digital teams, and external partners. You will work at the forefront of AI and digital innovation in a global healthcare company that is investing significantly in science and technology. The role offers the opportunity to shape how R&D operates, build new skills through cross-functional collaboration and grow your expertise at the intersection of science, AI and business.

You will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and contribute your expertise where it matters most. The work moves at pace, and curiosity, adaptability and a drive for impact are valued every day.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Development of High Temperature Heat Pumps with Thermal Energy Storage - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want to start your research career by making industrial heat clean, flexible and affordable? At DTU Construct you will work at the forefront of technologies key to decarbonizing industries: high-temperature heat pumps and high-temperature thermal energy storage.We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps and thermal energy storage. Your project will develop new Carnot Battery technologies: systems that combine heat pumps based on high temperature thermodynamic cycles together with high-temperature thermal energy storage, such as molten salts and dual-media packed beds. These systems will deliver clean process heat while also giving industry flexibility on the electricity market.Supervision: Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson with industrial secondments. Responsibilities and qualificationsYour overall goal will be to find out how industrial high temperature heat pumps can benefit from integrated thermal energy storage by developing new cost-effective, high-performance hybrid configurations. You will work with fellow doctoral candidates across the network and with industrial partners in Denmark and abroad.Your main tasks will be:
• Develop and Design new architectures comprising cycles using natural working fluids and thermal energy storage, optimised for efficiency, cost, and fast response to electricity price signals
• Carry out multi-objective optimisation and dynamic system analysis of alternative layouts
• Validate results by carrying out experiments and data comparison during industrial secondments, turning the results into innovations with real-world impact (e.g. patents, future commercial solutions) 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.You have:
• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.Approval and Enrolment The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. We offerDTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.Salary and appointment termsThe appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures. The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027, or according to mutual agreement. You can read more about career paths at DTU here.Further informationFurther information may be obtained from Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli, adrsc@dtu.dk and Prof. Anders Christiansen Erlandsson, acerl@dtu.dk. You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. Application procedure Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:
• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on high-temperature heat pumps combined with thermal energy storage (e.g. Carnot Batteries): select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making.You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
Are you motivated by making green commercial investments across Africa, Asia, and Latin America?

Impact Fund Denmark is Denmark’s largest impact fund and is internationally recognized as a best-in-class impact investor.  We manage our own private equity funds, debt capital, and concessional capital with a focus on creating sustainable businesses that deliver measurable social, economic and climate impact alongside solid financial returns.

We are strengthening our Green Energy and Infrastructure team and are looking for an Investment Professional to join us in our headquarters in Copenhagen. Depending on your experience, you may join us as Investment Analyst or Investment Manager.

Green Energy and Infrastructure invests in businesses and infrastructure that accelerate the green transition in emerging markets. Our investment focus spans renewable energy, circular economy, electric mobility, and water infrastructure. Through equity and debt investments, active ownership and strategic partnerships, we drive impact and value creation aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. We typically invest between DKK 100-350 million per transaction.

You will be reporting to a Managing Director in Green Energy and Infrastructure and work closely with colleagues in Copenhagen and our regional offices across Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America on investments throughout the investment lifecycle.

 

Investment Analyst

As an Investment Analyst, you will be a key analytical resource in transaction teams, focusing on commercial and financial analysis of investment opportunities.

You will:

• 
Screen and analyse new investment proposals using Impact Fund Denmark’s tools and processes.

• 
Assist in preparing investment papers, financial analyses and financial modelling.

• 
Support due diligence, valuation and deal structuring.

• 
Contribute to preparing and presenting investment recommendations and materials for the investment committee and board.

• 
Collect and analyse commercial and financial data for deal teams.

• 
Help maintain information systems for pipeline tracking and portfolio data.

• 
Participate in networking activities to support investment sourcing and promotion.

• 
Support project managers in active ownership and portfolio monitoring.

• 
Ensure timely and accurate updates of systems with project documents, and financial and sustainability reporting.

• 
Assist in assessing exit timing and support execution.

 

Qualifications:

• 
Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as finance or economics with strong academic results.

• 
1-2 years of relevant experience from impact investing, private equity, M&A, corporate finance or consulting.

• 
Solid understanding of financial analysis and valuation.

• 
Skilled user of Excel and with an interest in and aptitude for financial modelling.

• 
Detail-oriented with a structured working approach.

• 
Fluent in English (written and spoken).

• 
Curious to broaden your understanding of the world and keen to travel.

 

Investment Manager

As an Investment Manager, you will take the lead on many of the tasks performed by an Investment Analyst. You are thus expected to work independently, drive workstreams, and take ownership of parts of the investment process.

You will:

• 
Screen and analyse new investment proposals using Impact Fund Denmark’s tools and processes.

• 
Lead preparation of parts of investment papers, financial analyses and financial modelling with guidance from the project manager (Senior Investment Manager or Investment Director).

• 
Support and lead due diligence, valuation and deal structuring workstreams.

• 
Contribute to preparing and presenting investment recommendations and materials for the investment committee and board.

• 
Lead the analysis of commercial and financial data for deal teams.

• 
Take part in negotiating terms and drafting legal documentation.

• 
Help maintain information systems for pipeline tracking and portfolio data.

• 
Participate in networking activities to support investment sourcing and promotion.

• 
Support project managers in active ownership and portfolio monitoring.

• 
Assist in assessing exit timing and support exit negotiations and execution.

 

Qualifications:

• 
Master’s degree in a relevant field such as finance or economics with strong academic results.

• 
3-5 years of relevant experience from impact investing, private equity, M&A, corporate finance or consulting.

• 
Independent mindset and experienced in owning and managing workstreams.

• 
Solid understanding of financial analysis and valuation.

• 
Expert user of Excel and with an interest in and aptitude for financial modelling.

• 
Detail-oriented with a structured working approach.

• 
Fluent in English (written and spoken).

• 
Strong interpersonal skills and business judgment.

• 
Curious to broaden your understanding of the world and keen to travel.

• 
Experience in emerging markets and green energy is an advantage but not a prerequisite.

 

Working at Impact Fund Denmark

Learning is an important element of working in Impact Fund Denmark, and we will support your personal development through training, sparring and by ensuring that you get exciting and challenging tasks and new opportunities for growth. When joining Impact Fund Denmark, you will take part in our extensive onboarding program to get the best possible start in your new role.

We have a diverse and inclusive working environment with more than 170 talented individuals from 30+ different nationalities. We work seamlessly together with colleagues around the corner, across the organisation and between offices in Asia, Africa, Latin America and Europe.

About Impact Fund Denmark

Impact Fund Denmark (IFU – the Investment Fund for Developing Countries) is a Danish impact investor contributing to green, just and inclusive societies as well as supporting the Sustainable Development Goals. Impact Fund Denmark provides risk capital to companies operating in developing countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and parts of Europe. Investments are made on commercial terms in the form of equity, loans and guarantees. Impact Fund Denmark has co-invested in over 1,300 companies in more than 100 developing countries and emerging markets. Contracted investments total EUR 31 billion, of which Impact Fund Denmark has contributed EUR 3.4 billion. Capital under management will be growing from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 5.0 billion over the next few years. Read more at Impact Fund Denmark
